source.text: וַיַּעַל֩ אַבְרָ֨ם מִמִּצְרַ֜יִם ה֠וּא וְאִשְׁתּ֧וֹ וְכָל־אֲשֶׁר־ל֛וֹ וְל֥וֹט עִמּ֖וֹ הַנֶּֽגְבָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Abram from Egypt, he and his wife and all that [was] to him, and Lot with him, to the Negev.

en.L: And Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the Negev.
en.B: Abram left Egypt and went up to the Negev, taking his wife and all his possessions, and Lot came too.
en.R: Abram left Egypt and went back north to the Negev desert. His wife and Lot went with him, and he took everything he owned.

es.L: Y subió Abram de Egipto, él y su mujer y todo lo que tenía, y Lot con él, al Néguev.
es.B: Abram salió de Egipto y subió al Néguev con su mujer y todos sus bienes, y Lot fue también con él.
es.R: Abram salió de Egipto y volvió al norte, al desierto del Néguev. Su esposa y Lot fueron con él, y se llevó todo lo que tenía.

decisions.choice: went up: traveled north and uphill
decisions.reason: Going from Egypt to Canaan is always "going up", as going to Egypt is "going down" (12:10): the land rises toward the hill country.

source.text: וְאַבְרָ֖ם כָּבֵ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד בַּמִּקְנֶ֕ה בַּכֶּ֖סֶף וּבַזָּהָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And Abram [was] heavy very in livestock, in silver and in gold.

en.L: And Abram [was] very rich in livestock, in silver and in gold.
en.B: By now Abram was a very rich man, with herds and flocks, silver and gold.
en.R: Abram was very rich. He had many animals and a lot of silver and gold.

es.L: Y Abram [era] muy rico en ganado, en plata y en oro.
es.B: Para entonces Abram era muy rico: tenía ganado, plata y oro.
es.R: Abram era muy rico. Tenía muchos animales y mucha plata y oro.

decisions.choice: heavy: rich
decisions.reason: The word means heavy, and so rich or weighty. It is the root of "glory" (kavod). Abram's wealth comes partly from Egypt (12:16) and sets up the quarrel that follows.

source.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ לְמַסָּעָ֔יו מִנֶּ֖גֶב וְעַד־בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל עַד־הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁר־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֤ם אָֽהֳלוֹ֙ בַּתְּחִלָּ֔ה בֵּ֥ין בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל וּבֵ֥ין הָעָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went by his stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where had been his tent at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,

en.L: And he went on by stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
en.B: From the Negev he traveled in stages back to Bethel, to the spot between Bethel and Ai where he had first pitched his tent,
en.R: From the Negev he moved from place to place until he came back to the place between Bethel and Ai where he had first put up his tent.

es.L: Y fue por etapas desde el Néguev hasta Betel, hasta el lugar donde había estado su tienda al principio, entre Betel y Hai,
es.B: Desde el Néguev fue avanzando por etapas hasta Betel, al lugar entre Betel y Hai donde había plantado su tienda la primera vez,
es.R: Desde el Néguev fue de un lugar a otro hasta que volvió al sitio entre Betel y Hai donde había puesto su tienda la primera vez.

decisions.choice: at the beginning: back where he started
decisions.reason: Abram returns to the place where he first camped and built an altar (12:8). After the failure in Egypt he goes back to the place of worship.

source.text: אֶל־מְקוֹם֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ אֲשֶׁר־עָ֥שָׂה שָׁ֖ם בָּרִאשֹׁנָ֑ה וַיִּקְרָ֥א שָׁ֛ם אַבְרָ֖ם בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: to [the] place of the altar which he had made there at the first; and called there Abram on [the] name of YHWH.

en.L: to the place of the altar that he had made there at first; and there Abram called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: where he had built the altar before. There Abram called on the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: This was where he had built an altar. There Abram prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} again.

es.L: al lugar del altar que allí había hecho antes; e invocó allí Abram el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: donde antes había construido el altar. Allí Abram invocó el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Era el lugar donde había construido un altar. Allí Abram oró otra vez {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y adoró {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} nombre.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}
decisions.reason: First occurrence in this chapter, as in 2:4: the divine name is "el SEÑOR" in small capitals by default, with "Yahvé" as a reader setting. The span takes in the article and any contraction ("del SEÑOR" / "de Yahvé", "al SEÑOR" / "a Yahvé").

decisions.choice: invocó el nombre del SEÑOR (L, B); oró al SEÑOR y adoró su nombre (R)
decisions.reason: Abram returns to the worship of 12:8, and each level repeats the Spanish of 12:8 (and 4:26). Readable adds "y adoró su nombre" where the English Readable says only "prayed"; "su" carries the deity pronoun setting.

source.text: וְגַם־לְל֔וֹט הַהֹלֵ֖ךְ אֶת־אַבְרָ֑ם הָיָ֥ה צֹאן־וּבָקָ֖ר וְאֹהָלִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And also to Lot, who went with Abram, belonged sheep and cattle and tents.

en.L: And Lot also, who went with Abram, had flocks and herds and tents.
en.B: Lot, traveling with Abram, had his own flocks and herds and tents as well.
en.R: Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had sheep, cattle and tents.

es.L: Y también Lot, que iba con Abram, tenía ovejas y reses y tiendas.
es.B: Lot, que acompañaba a Abram, tenía también sus propios rebaños de ovejas y de vacas, y sus tiendas.
es.R: Lot, que viajaba con Abram, también tenía ovejas, vacas y tiendas.

decisions.choice: tents: households
decisions.reason: "Tents" stands for the households living in them, servants and herdsmen included.

source.text: וְלֹא־נָשָׂ֥א אֹתָ֛ם הָאָ֖רֶץ לָשֶׁ֣בֶת יַחְדָּ֑ו כִּֽי־הָיָ֤ה רְכוּשָׁם֙ רָ֔ב וְלֹ֥א יָֽכְל֖וּ לָשֶׁ֥בֶת יַחְדָּֽו׃

records.literal_gloss: And not supported them the land to dwell together, for was their possessions much, and not they were able to dwell together.

en.L: And the land could not support them dwelling together, for their possessions were so great that they could not dwell together.
en.B: The land could not sustain both of them living side by side; they had so much that they could not stay together.
en.R: There was not enough grass and water for both of them to live in the same place, because they had too many animals.

es.L: Y la tierra no podía sostenerlos para que habitaran juntos, porque sus posesiones eran tantas que no podían habitar juntos.
es.B: La tierra no daba para que los dos vivieran uno al lado del otro; tenían tantos bienes que no podían quedarse juntos.
es.R: No había suficiente pasto ni agua para que los dos vivieran en el mismo lugar, porque tenían demasiados animales.

decisions.choice: the land could not support them: not enough pasture and water
decisions.reason: Herds need grazing land and wells. Two large households in one area compete for both. The blessing of wealth itself brings strain.

source.text: וַֽיְהִי־רִ֗יב בֵּ֚ין רֹעֵ֣י מִקְנֵֽה־אַבְרָ֔ם וּבֵ֖ין רֹעֵ֣י מִקְנֵה־ל֑וֹט וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י אָ֖ז יֹשֵׁ֥ב בָּאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was strife between [the] herdsmen of [the] livestock of Abram and between [the] herdsmen of [the] livestock of Lot; and the Canaanite[s] and the Perizzite[s] then dwelt in the land.

en.L: And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram's livestock and the herdsmen of Lot's livestock. And the Canaanites and the Perizzites were then living in the land.
en.B: Before long Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen were at odds with each other. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were also settled in the land.
en.R: The men who looked after Abram's animals began to quarrel with the men who looked after Lot's animals. The Canaanites and the Perizzites also lived in the land then.

es.L: Y hubo contienda entre quienes pastoreaban el ganado de Abram y quienes pastoreaban el ganado de Lot. Y los cananeos y los ferezeos habitaban entonces en la tierra.
es.B: Al poco tiempo, los pastores de Abram y los de Lot andaban enfrentados. En aquel tiempo también estaban establecidos en la tierra los cananeos y los ferezeos.
es.R: Los hombres que cuidaban los animales de Abram empezaron a pelear con los que cuidaban los animales de Lot. En ese tiempo también vivían en aquella tierra los cananeos y los ferezeos.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites and Perizzites were living in the land: little room, and watching neighbors
decisions.reason: The note explains why there was so little room, and it may hint that the quarrel was a poor witness before the people of the land. The Perizzites may have been village dwellers of the hill country.

decisions.choice: los ferezeos
decisions.reason: The traditional Spanish form of the name, used by most Spanish Bibles; gentilics are written in lower case, like "los cananeos".

decisions.choice: contienda (L, also in 13:8); andaban enfrentados (B, 13:7), pleitos (B, 13:8)
decisions.reason: The same word stands in 13:7 and 13:8, so Literal uses one Spanish word for both, "contienda", the usual word for a quarrel between parties. Balanced varies it as the English Balanced does ("at odds", "quarrel"); Readable says "pelear".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אַבְרָ֜ם אֶל־ל֗וֹט אַל־נָ֨א תְהִ֤י מְרִיבָה֙ בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֔יךָ וּבֵ֥ין רֹעַ֖י וּבֵ֣ין רֹעֶ֑יךָ כִּֽי־אֲנָשִׁ֥ים אַחִ֖ים אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Abram to Lot, let there not be, please, strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for men brothers we [are].

en.L: And Abram said to Lot, "Please let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we [are] kinsmen.
en.B: So Abram said to Lot, "There should be no quarrel between us, or between your herdsmen and mine. We are family.
en.R: So Abram said to Lot, "We should not quarrel, and our men should not quarrel either. We are family.

es.L: Y dijo Abram a Lot: «No haya, por favor, contienda entre tú y yo, ni entre mis pastores y tus pastores, porque [somos] parientes.
es.B: Así que Abram le dijo a Lot: «No debe haber pleitos entre nosotros, ni entre tus pastores y los míos. Somos familia.
es.R: Entonces Abram le dijo a Lot: «No debemos pelear, y nuestros hombres tampoco deben pelear. Somos familia.

decisions.choice: we are brothers: we are close kin
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is used of any close relatives; Lot is Abram's nephew (11:27). Abram, the elder, takes the first step toward peace.

source.text: הֲלֹ֤א כָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ הִפָּ֥רֶד נָ֖א מֵעָלָ֑י אִם־הַשְּׂמֹ֣אל וְאֵימִ֔נָה וְאִם־הַיָּמִ֖ין וְאַשְׂמְאִֽילָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Is not all the land before you? Separate, please, from me; if the left, then I will go right, and if the right, then I will go left.

en.L: Is not the whole land before you? Please separate from me. If [you take] the left, then I will go to the right; or if the right, then I will go to the left."
en.B: The whole land is open to you. Let us go our separate ways. You take the left and I will take the right, or you take the right and I will take the left."
en.R: Look at all the land in front of you. Let us go different ways. You choose first. If you go one way, I will go the other way."

es.L: ¿No [está] toda la tierra ante ti? Sepárate, por favor, de mí. Si [tomas] la izquierda, yo iré a la derecha; y si la derecha, yo iré a la izquierda».
es.B: Toda la tierra está a tu disposición. Separémonos. Si tú tomas la izquierda, yo tomaré la derecha; si tomas la derecha, yo tomaré la izquierda».
es.R: Mira toda la tierra que tienes delante. Vámonos cada uno por su lado. Tú eliges primero. Si vas por un lado, yo me iré por el otro».

decisions.choice: if the left, I will go right: Abram gives Lot the first choice
decisions.reason: As the elder and the one to whom the land was promised (12:7), Abram had the right to choose. He gives it up, trusting God's promise. "Left" and "right" can also mean north and south, as a person faces east.

decisions.choice: ¿No [está] toda la tierra ante ti?
alternatives: ¿No es toda la tierra ante ti?
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb. The English Literal can say "Is not" without a bracket, but Spanish needs "estar" for location, so Literal supplies "[está]".

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂא־ל֣וֹט אֶת־עֵינָ֗יו וַיַּרְא֙ אֶת־כָּל־כִּכַּ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן כִּ֥י כֻלָּ֖הּ מַשְׁקֶ֑ה לִפְנֵ֣י׀שַׁחֵ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־סְדֹם֙ וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֔ה כְּגַן־יְהוָה֙ כְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בֹּאֲכָ֖ה צֹֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And lifted Lot his eyes and saw all [the] plain of the Jordan, that all of it [was] well-watered, before YHWH destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like [the] garden of YHWH, like [the] land of Egypt, as you go to Zoar.

en.L: And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw all the plain of the Jordan, that it was all well watered, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, like the land of Egypt, in the direction of Zoar.
en.B: Lot looked out over the Jordan plain and saw water everywhere, all the way to Zoar, as in the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or the land of Egypt. (That was before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.)
en.R: Lot looked around and saw that the whole Jordan valley, as far as Zoar, had plenty of water. It was like the garden of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or like the land of Egypt. (This was before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.)

es.L: Y levantó Lot sus ojos y miró toda la llanura del Jordán, que estaba bien regada toda ella, antes de que destruyera {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Sodoma y a Gomorra, como el jardín {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, como la tierra de Egipto, yendo hacia Zoar.
es.B: Lot contempló la llanura del Jordán y vio que había agua por todas partes, hasta Zoar, como en el jardín {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} o en la tierra de Egipto. (Esto fue antes de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} destruyera Sodoma y Gomorra.)
es.R: Lot miró a su alrededor y vio que todo el valle del Jordán, hasta Zoar, tenía mucha agua. Era como el jardín {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} o como la tierra de Egipto. (Esto pasó antes de que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} destruyera las ciudades de Sodoma y Gomorra.)

decisions.choice: the plain of the Jordan: the circle of land around the lower Jordan
decisions.reason: The word means a circle or round area: the valley of the Jordan near the Dead Sea, then fertile and well watered.

decisions.choice: like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt: attractive, and dangerous
decisions.reason: The plain looks like Eden and like Egypt, both places of plenty. But the note "before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah" warns the reader what lies ahead (chapter 19).

decisions.choice: the note about Sodom in brackets at the end
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move the narrator's aside to the end of the sentence and set it in brackets, so the description reads clearly.

decisions.choice: la llanura del Jordán (L, B), el valle del Jordán (R); el jardín del SEÑOR
decisions.reason: The word means a round area (m1); Spanish follows the English per level, "llanura" for "plain" and "valle" for the Readable "valley", and keeps the same words in 13:11–12. The garden is the word of chapters 2–3, rendered "jardín" there, so the comparison with Eden stays visible (m2).

source.text: וַיִּבְחַר־ל֣וֹ ל֗וֹט אֵ֚ת כָּל־כִּכַּ֣ר הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וַיִּסַּ֥ע ל֖וֹט מִקֶּ֑דֶם וַיִּפָּ֣רְד֔וּ אִ֖ישׁ מֵעַ֥ל אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And chose for himself Lot all [the] plain of the Jordan, and set out Lot eastward, and they separated each from his brother.

en.L: And Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot set out eastward; and they separated from each other.
en.B: So Lot chose the whole Jordan plain for himself and moved off to the east. The two of them parted.
en.R: So Lot chose the Jordan valley for himself and moved east. That is how Abram and Lot separated.

es.L: Y eligió para sí Lot toda la llanura del Jordán, y se marchó Lot hacia el oriente; y se separaron el uno del otro.
es.B: Lot eligió entonces toda la llanura del Jordán para sí y se fue hacia el oriente. Los dos se separaron.
es.R: Entonces Lot se quedó con el valle del Jordán y se fue hacia el este. Así fue como Abram y Lot se separaron.

decisions.choice: eastward: moving east again
decisions.reason: In Genesis, going east has marked moving away from God's presence (3:24; 4:16; 11:2). Lot chooses by what his eyes see.

source.text: אַבְרָ֖ם יָשַׁ֣ב בְּאֶֽרֶץ־כְּנָ֑עַן וְל֗וֹט יָשַׁב֙ בְּעָרֵ֣י הַכִּכָּ֔ר וַיֶּאֱהַ֖ל עַד־סְדֹֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Abram dwelt in [the] land of Canaan, and Lot dwelt in [the] cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.

en.L: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot settled among the cities of the plain and pitched his tent as far as Sodom.
en.B: Abram remained in Canaan; Lot settled among the towns of the plain and moved his camp as far as Sodom.
en.R: Abram stayed in Canaan. Lot lived among the towns in the valley and moved his tents close to Sodom.

es.L: Abram se estableció en la tierra de Canaán, y Lot se estableció entre las ciudades de la llanura y fue plantando su tienda hasta Sodoma.
es.B: Abram se quedó en Canaán; Lot se estableció entre las ciudades de la llanura y trasladó su campamento hasta Sodoma.
es.R: Abram se quedó en Canaán. Lot vivió entre las ciudades del valle y llevó sus tiendas cerca de Sodoma.

decisions.choice: as far as Sodom: drawing near to danger
decisions.reason: Lot moves his tent step by step toward Sodom; by 14:12 he lives in it, and by 19:1 he sits in its gate.

decisions.choice: fue plantando su tienda hasta Sodoma
decisions.reason: The verb is "to tent", moving and pitching the tent; Literal uses the Spanish progressive "fue plantando" to show the camp moving stage by stage toward Sodom (m1), where the English Literal says "pitched his tent as far as".

source.text: וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י סְדֹ֔ם רָעִ֖ים וְחַטָּאִ֑ים לַיהוָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And the men of Sodom [were] evil and sinners against YHWH exceedingly.

en.L: Now the men of Sodom were wicked, great sinners against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The people of Sodom, however, were evil and grievous sinners against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: The people of Sodom were very wicked. They sinned terribly against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y los hombres de Sodoma [eran] malvados y grandes pecadores contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Los habitantes de Sodoma, sin embargo, eran malvados y pecaban gravemente contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Los que vivían en Sodoma eran muy malos. Pecaban terriblemente contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: wicked, great sinners against the LORD: the warning sounded
decisions.reason: The narrator's comment explains the destruction to come (18:20; 19:4-13). Ezekiel 16:49-50 describes Sodom's sins as pride, excess and neglect of the poor, together with detestable acts.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The word can refer to the inhabitants generally; Balanced and Readable say "people", Literal keeps "men".

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֞ה אָמַ֣ר אֶל־אַבְרָ֗ם אַחֲרֵי֙ הִפָּֽרֶד־ל֣וֹט מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֨יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֣ה שָׁ֑ם צָפֹ֥נָה וָנֶ֖גְבָּה וָקֵ֥דְמָה וָיָֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And YHWH said to Abram after had separated Lot from him, lift up, please, your eyes and see from the place where you [are], northward and southward and eastward and westward,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, "Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,
en.B: After Lot had gone, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Raise your eyes and look out from where you stand, to the north and south, east and west.
en.R: After Lot left, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Abram, "Look around you in every direction: north, south, east and west.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Abram, después que Lot se separó de él: «Levanta tus ojos y, desde el lugar en que estás, mira hacia el norte y hacia el sur y hacia el oriente y hacia el occidente,
es.B: Cuando Lot ya se había ido, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Abram: «Alza la vista y mira desde donde estás, al norte y al sur, al oriente y al occidente.
es.R: Después de que Lot se fue, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Abram: «Mira a tu alrededor, hacia todos lados: al norte, al sur, al este y al oeste.

decisions.choice: lift up your eyes: God shows Abram what Lot saw for himself
decisions.reason: Lot "lifted up his eyes" and chose for himself (verse 10). Now God tells Abram to lift up his eyes, and gives him everything he sees.

source.text: כִּ֧י אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֛רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְךָ֣ אֶתְּנֶ֑נָּה וּֽלְזַרְעֲךָ֖ עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For all the land that you are seeing, to you I will give it, and to your offspring forever.

en.L: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.
en.B: I am giving you all the land you can see, to you and your descendants for all time.
en.R: I will give all the land you can see to you and to your family after you, forever.

es.L: porque toda la tierra que tú ves, a ti te la daré, y a tu descendencia para siempre.
es.B: Toda la tierra que alcanzas a ver te la doy a ti y a tus descendientes, para siempre.
es.R: Toda la tierra que puedes ver te la daré a ti y a los de tu familia que vengan después de ti, para siempre.

decisions.choice: forever: for all time to come
decisions.reason: The word (olam) means a very long or unlimited time. The promise is lasting.

decisions.choice: descendencia (L), descendientes (B), los de tu familia que vengan después de ti (R)
alternatives: tus hijos y los hijos de ellos
decisions.reason: As in 12:7, Literal says "descendencia" and Balanced "descendientes" (also in 13:16). Readable follows the English Readable here ("your family after you") rather than repeating the "tus hijos y los hijos de ellos" of 12:7.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֥י אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֖ כַּעֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֑רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀אִם־יוּכַ֣ל אִ֗ישׁ לִמְנוֹת֙ אֶת־עֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ גַּֽם־זַרְעֲךָ֖ יִמָּנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make your offspring like [the] dust of the earth, so that if one is able to count the dust of the earth, also your offspring could be counted.

en.L: And I will make your offspring like the dust of the earth, so that if anyone could count the dust of the earth, your offspring also could be counted.
en.B: I will make your descendants as countless as the dust of the earth; only if someone could count the dust could your descendants be counted.
en.R: I will give you so many descendants that they will be like the dust of the earth. No one can count the dust, and no one will be able to count your descendants.

es.L: Y haré tu descendencia como el polvo de la tierra, de modo que, si alguien pudiera contar el polvo de la tierra, podría contarse también tu descendencia.
es.B: Haré que tus descendientes sean tan incontables como el polvo de la tierra; solo si alguien pudiera contar el polvo, podrían contarse tus descendientes.
es.R: Te daré tantos descendientes que serán como el polvo de la tierra. Nadie puede contar el polvo, y nadie podrá contar a tus descendientes.

decisions.choice: like the dust of the earth: beyond counting
decisions.reason: Later God compares Abram's descendants to the stars (15:5) and the sand (22:17): pictures of numbers beyond counting, made to a man with no child.

source.text: ק֚וּם הִתְהַלֵּ֣ךְ בָּאָ֔רֶץ לְאָרְכָּ֖הּ וּלְרָחְבָּ֑הּ כִּ֥י לְךָ֖ אֶתְּנֶֽנָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Arise, walk about in the land, through its length and its breadth, for to you I will give it.

en.L: Arise, walk through the land, its length and its breadth, for I will give it to you."
en.B: Go and travel the land from end to end and side to side, because I am giving it to you."
en.R: Go and walk through the whole land, from one end to the other, because I am giving it to you."

es.L: Levántate, recorre la tierra en su longitud y en su anchura, porque a ti te la daré».
es.B: Ve y recorre la tierra de un extremo a otro y de lado a lado, porque yo te la doy».
es.R: Ve y camina por toda la tierra, de un extremo al otro, porque te la doy a ti».

decisions.choice: walk through the land: as an owner surveys his property
decisions.reason: Walking through a land could be a way of taking possession of it (Joshua 1:3). Abram is to explore what will be his.

source.text: וַיֶּאֱהַ֣ל אַבְרָ֗ם וַיָּבֹ֛א וַיֵּ֛שֶׁב בְּאֵלֹנֵ֥י מַמְרֵ֖א אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּחֶבְר֑וֹן וַיִּֽבֶן־שָׁ֥ם מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And moved his tent Abram and came and dwelt at [the] great trees of Mamre, which [are] at Hebron, and he built there an altar to YHWH.

en.L: And Abram moved his tent and came and settled by the great trees of Mamre, which are at Hebron, and he built there an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So Abram moved his tents and went to live near the great trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: So Abram moved his tents and went to live by the big trees of Mamre, near the town of Hebron. There he built an altar to worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y trasladó Abram su tienda, y vino y habitó junto a las encinas de Mamre, que están en Hebrón, y edificó allí un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.B: Así que Abram trasladó sus tiendas y se fue a vivir junto a las encinas de Mamre, en Hebrón, donde construyó un altar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces Abram llevó sus tiendas a las grandes encinas de Mamre, cerca de la ciudad de Hebrón, y se quedó a vivir allí. En ese lugar construyó un altar para adorar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.

decisions.choice: the great trees of Mamre at Hebron: Abram's home in the hill country
decisions.reason: Mamre, near Hebron in the southern hill country, becomes Abraham's main home (14:13; 18:1). Sarah and Abraham are buried nearby (23:19; 25:9).

decisions.choice: las encinas de Mamre (L, B); las grandes encinas de Mamre (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the plural of the tree of 12:6, so Spanish uses the plural of "la encina de More"; Readable adds "grandes" as the English Readable says "big trees".
